fetched 2026-09-11, unmodified, MIT licence (see file headers)
local modification 2026-09-13 (exp.c only): the two bare `asm("":"=x"(r):"0"(x))`
statements (near the GCC branches of the sign/underflow helpers) are spelled
`__asm__` — `asm` is not a keyword under -std=c11 (depends/hosts/mingw32.mk
compiles C that way for the Windows build) while `__asm__` is accepted by every
GCC/Clang mode, exactly as the file's own lines 56-60 already do. No
arithmetic or codegen change (the asm string is empty; it is a register
reinterpretation). The byte-identical copy in shared-utils/pow-utils/coremath/
exp.c must carry the same two-character change.
local modification 2026-09-13 (exp.c only): the `roundeven_finite` selector
additionally requires `!defined(__MINGW32__)`. With gcc >= 10 the file maps
roundeven_finite to __builtin_roundeven; on x86-64 without SSE4.1 gcc lowers
that builtin to a call to libm `roundeven`, which the mingw-w64 CRT does not
provide, so the Windows (mingw32 depends) link of bitcoin-qt failed with two
undefined references to `roundeven` from exp.c.obj. MinGW builds now take the
file's own portable branch (`__builtin_round` + ties-to-even correction, the
branch upstream already uses for MSVC and pre-10 gcc); `round` is in the
mingw-w64 CRT. Every other platform is preprocessor-identical to before. The
portable branch returns +0 where roundeven returns -0 (x = -0.5 exactly); at
both call sites t feeds only (i64)t and products with x subtracted, where the
sign of zero is inert, and a whole-function differential run of cr_exp
(default branch vs forced portable branch) over ties, the -0.5/s
neighbourhood and 2x10^7 random arguments was bit-identical. The
byte-identical copy in shared-utils/pow-utils/coremath/exp.c must carry the
same change.
